archetype.name: Fringe Contender (run-first, special-teams-propped)
archetype.definition: A .500 team whose efficiency ranks in the bottom third and whose playoff case rests on Jonathan Taylor, elite special teams, clean football and a soft division and schedule rather than on how well it plays snap to snap.

report.headline: Taylor and special teams are carrying a passing game that isn't working
report.take:
Indianapolis is 2-2 with a -2 point differential, so the record is honest about the scoreboard. The underlying play is a notch worse. Net EPA ranks 23rd, yardage ranks 26th on offense and 31st on defense, and the turnover margin is 31st at -1.5 per game. This is not last year's Colts. In 2025 the offense ranked 7th in EPA, and this year it is 23rd. The drop is almost entirely in the air: pass EPA is 30th, and Daniel Jones has averaged under 190 passing yards a game, with a passing EPA below zero in three of four starts.

What keeps the team afloat is a strange but real combination. The run game is the best in the league by EPA (0.121, 1st), with a 4th-ranked stuff rate and a 46.7% success rate, and Taylor has taken 86 of the backfield's carries. It is a Taylor operation more than a line one. Yards before contact rank 29th, so the backs are earning their yards after first contact. Special teams add 4.34 EPA a game (2nd), and the Colts commit the fewest penalties in the league. That explains how a team 26th in yards scores 25.5 points a game (13th). Week 4 is the clearest example: 30 points on 271 yards while the passing game posted -13.4 EPA.

The numbers hide a few things. The 25.5 points overstate the offense, because hidden yardage from the kicking game and field position is doing work that drives aren't. The defense's 4th-ranked third-down rate (29.2%) sits on top of a 28th-ranked pressure rate and 27th-ranked missed-tackle rate. That combination usually lets drives stay alive later in the year. The defensive splits also depend on the opponent. BAL and KC, both top-five offenses, put up 74 points and 1,060 yards. HOU and WAS, ranked 20th and 21st, managed 30 points. The turnover margin cuts the other way. Eight giveaways in four games is more fumbling of possessions than this offense's profile fully explains, and the two takeaways (28th) should drift upward. Some of that luck should come back toward the Colts.

The path forward is friendlier than the efficiency. Two games with 0-4 Tennessee, plus Houston and Miami (both 0-4), and a Philadelphia team with a 29th-ranked offense give this team a realistic route to nine wins without fixing much. The hard part is the receiving corps. Keenan Allen is out with a groin injury and Alec Pierce is on IR until around Week 8, which leaves Josh Downs, Tyler Warren and Laquon Treadwell as the targets. Until one of them returns, the passing game is unlikely to climb out of the bottom five.

strengths.title: Taylor-driven run game leads the league
strengths.body: Indy's rush EPA and run success rate are both elite, and the stuff rate is 4th despite yards before contact ranking 29th. That points to the back creating more than the line opening holes. Production that comes from the runner rather than the blocking tends to hold up, and it has been positive in three of four games. The risk is volume: 21-plus carries a week depends on staying in close games.

strengths.title: Special teams swing field position
strengths.body: At 4.34 EPA per game, the third phase is worth close to a field goal a week. It is the main reason the Colts score at a 13th-ranked rate on 26th-ranked yardage. Special-teams EPA is noisier than offense or defense, so expect some cooling. A unit this far ahead of the league is likely still a real plus.

strengths.title: Clean, disciplined football
strengths.body: The Colts commit the fewest penalties in the league and rank 2nd in line penalties. Pass protection has also held up, with a 6th-ranked pressure rate allowed despite a slow 2.73-second time to throw. Discipline is usually a coaching trait and tends to persist.

concerns.title: Passing game near the bottom
concerns.body: Pass EPA is 30th, with -13.4 at Washington and -9.6 against Baltimore. This is a real flaw, not a game-script artifact. Pass rate over expected is neutral, so Indy isn't being forced into bad passing situations. Allen and Pierce being out makes it worse in the near term, and this is a steep fall from a 7th-ranked offense in 2025.

concerns.title: Turnover margin bleeding possessions
concerns.body: Eight giveaways against two takeaways in four games puts the Colts 31st in turnover differential. Some of it is the struggling passing game, but three giveaways in a win over Houston and a 28th-ranked takeaway total both look extreme. Expect the margin to improve toward neutral rather than stay this bad.

concerns.title: No pass rush, and fewer rushers
concerns.body: A 28th-ranked pressure rate and 27th-ranked missed-tackle rate are why yardage allowed ranks 31st. The 4th-ranked third-down defense is unlikely to keep covering for that. Arden Key, a 65%-snap edge rusher, is out, and Micheal Clemons is on IR, so the rush gets thinner before it gets better.

trend.note: Results have improved from 0-2 to 2-2, but the passing game has swung from +5.9 EPA at KC to -13.4 at Washington. The wins came on the ground, through special teams and against weaker offenses rather than from a steadily improving team.

nextGame.headline: Near coin flip in Pittsburgh hinges on Taylor and ball security
nextGame.body:
Pittsburgh is a mirror image in quality: also 2-2, net EPA 21st to Indy's 23rd, with a bottom-ten passing offense (27th) that still throws at the 3rd-highest rate over expected. The Steelers' line allows the 2nd-highest pressure rate in the league, a weakness the Colts' 28th-ranked rush is poorly equipped to exploit. On the other side, Pittsburgh's defense is strong against short passes (8th) but leaky deep (27th) and tackles poorly (29th). That suits Taylor far better than it suits a Jones passing game short on outside targets.

Availability tilts both ways. Indy is without Key and Allen, with Pierce and Clemons on IR, so the passing game and the pass rush are both short-handed. Pittsburgh is likely without cornerback Jamel Dean (doubtful, 73% snaps), has interior lineman Derrick Harmon on IR and running back Rico Dowdle ruled out. The Dean and Harmon absences hit exactly the areas Indy wants to attack: the secondary and the run defense.

keyMatchups.title: Taylor against Pittsburgh's poor tackling
keyMatchups.body: Indy's run game wins after contact, and Pittsburgh misses tackles at the 4th-worst rate while allowing a 23rd-ranked success rate. With Harmon on IR, the Steelers' interior is thinner too. If Taylor gets his usual 20-plus carries, Indy can control the game without asking much of Jones.

keyMatchups.title: Colts giveaways against Steelers takeaways
keyMatchups.body: Pittsburgh ranks 6th in takeaways, and the Colts have given the ball away at least once every week. This is the factor most likely to flip a game priced within a field goal.

keyMatchups.title: Special teams and discipline edge
keyMatchups.body: Indy adds 4.34 special-teams EPA a game to Pittsburgh's -0.26, and commits 4 penalties a game to the Steelers' 6.3. In a game between two below-average offenses, those hidden yards are worth about a field goal.

nextGame.watch: Whether Indy reaches halftime without a giveaway: if it does, a Taylor-heavy script against Pittsburgh's tackling should keep this a one-score game it can win.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the scoring to cool toward the low 20s as the special-teams boost settles and as the points-per-yard rate drifts back toward the yardage. Expect the turnover margin to improve, which partly offsets that. The run game should stay a top-five unit. The passing game's best hope is Allen's return and Pierce coming back around Week 8, and even then a 30th-ranked pass offense more likely climbs to the low 20s than to average. The defense's third-down success is the most fragile number on the sheet, so points allowed probably stay in the mid-20s.

The schedule is the Colts' best friend. TEN twice, HOU and MIA are all 0-4 teams with bottom-ten offenses, and PHI and NYG are beatable. MIN (1st-ranked defense), JAX twice and DAL's 2nd-ranked offense are the tough draws. A 6-7 finish over the last 13 games is the median, and in a division where two teams are 0-4, that keeps Indy in the race.
swingFactors: Allen and Pierce returning to lift the passing game
Turnover margin moving back toward even
Whether the third-down defense holds without a pass rush

bets.reason: The teams grade nearly identically by net EPA (-0.087 vs -0.069). Indy brings a roughly 4.6-EPA-per-game special-teams edge, far fewer penalties, and a run game that fits Pittsburgh's 29th-ranked tackling and Harmon's absence. The turnover matchup against PIT's 6th-ranked takeaway defense is the main risk.

Both passing offenses rank near the bottom (30th and 27th by EPA), and the Colts lean on a clock-controlling run game. Indy's 25.5 points a game outrun its 26th-ranked yardage. Pittsburgh's 27th-ranked deep defense is the main threat to the under, and Indy is short on the receivers to exploit it.

confidence.note: Only four games, but the profile has held every week: strong run game, weak passing and leaky yardage. Receiver injuries add uncertainty.
